questions.question: Which National Waterway runs from Haldia to Prayagraj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Waterway 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Waterway 1** runs from **Haldia to Prayagraj**.
 
• The National Waterway 1 (NW-1), also known as the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system, spans from Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh to Haldia in West Bengal, traversing through Patna and Bhagalpur in Bihar along the Ganges river.
 
• Stretching over 1,620 km (1,010 mi), NW-1 holds the distinction of being India's longest waterway.
 
• Renowned for its strategic location, NW-1 passes through several states including West Bengal, Jharkhand, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh, connecting major cities
 
• Designated as a national waterway in October 1986, NW-1 facilitates navigation by mechanical boats up to Patna, playing a pivotal role in inland water transportation in India.

Officially designated as NW-2 on September 1, 1988, this waterway plays a crucial role in inland navigation in the northeastern region of India.
 
• **National Waterway 3 (NW-3) **spans 205 kilometers and serves as an inland navigational route in Kerala, India. Running from Kollam to Kottapuram, NW-3 was declared a National Waterway in 1993, facilitating transportation and trade within the state of Kerala.
 
• **National Waterway 4 (NW-4)** covers a distance of 1,095 kilometers, linking the Indian states of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and the union territory of Puducherry. This waterway connects the Krishna and Godavari rivers, serving as a vital transportation route for cargo and passenger movement in the region.

questions.question: What is the approx width of broad-gauge railway network in India?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The width of the broad-gauge railway network in India is approximately **1.6 metres (5 feet 6 inches)**.
 
• Broad gauge is the most widely used railway gauge in India, making up about **80% of the total railway network**.
 
• The broad-gauge tracks are used for both freight and passenger trains due to their stability and ability to handle higher speeds and heavier loads.
 
• It was first introduced in the mid-19th century during the British colonial period and has since become the standard gauge in India.

• **Metre Gauge:** Approximately 1 metre (3 feet 3 3⁄8 inches) wide, used in some regional and rural areas.
 
• **Narrow Gauge:** Less than 1 metre wide, including gauges of 2 feet 6 inches and 2 feet, primarily used in hilly and difficult terrains.
 
• **Standard Gauge:** 1.435 metres (4 feet 8 1⁄2 inches) wide, used for metro and high-speed rail projects.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Broad Gauge**
 
 
• Increased stability and capacity for heavier and faster trains.
 
• Reduced transportation costs due to the ability to carry more freight.
 
• Better passenger comfort due to wider coaches and more space.
 
 
 
• **Historical Development**
 
 
• Railways were introduced to India in 1853 during British rule.
 
• The first railway line connected Bombay (now Mumbai) and Thane.
 
• Since then, the network has expanded significantly, integrating various gauge types.

• **Border roads** are the roads constructed on the **North** and **North Eastern** borders of the country, constructed and maintained by the **Border Roads Organization **(BRO).

questions.question: In India, roads are classified in the _____ classes according to their capacity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**six**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The classification of roads in India** is based on the capacity of the road. This means that the number of lanes, width, and design of the road are all taken into account to determine its capacity.
 
• There are **six classes of roads in India**, with Class 1 being the highest capacity and Class 6 being the lowest. Class 1 roads are typically expressways or highways, while Class 6 roads are rural roads or village roads.
 
• The classification of roads is important for planning and development purposes. It helps policymakers to determine where to invest in infrastructure and which roads are in most need of improvement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• In India, the classification of roads is based on the recommendations of the Indian Roads Congress (IRC). The IRC is a professional organization that provides guidance and standards for road development in India.
 
• Class 1 roads are typically expressways or highways that connect major cities and are designed for high-speed traffic. Class 2 roads are also highways but are designed for slightly lower speeds and connect smaller towns and cities.
 
• Class 3 roads are major district roads that connect smaller towns and villages. Class 4 roads are other district roads that connect rural areas. Class 5 roads are village roads that connect individual villages. Class 6 roads are rural roads that provide access to individual homes and farms.

It is serviced by 13 major ports (12 Government-owned and one private) and 187 notified minor and intermediate ports.

First corporatized port of India:

__
 
• Kamarajar port located at Ennore in Tamil Nadu is the only corporate port owned by the Indian government.
 
• Kamarajar Port Ltd was formed as a company under the Companies Act when it was opened in 2001.
 
• Ennore Port is located on the Coromandel Coast about 18 km north of Chennai Port, Chennai, it is the 12th major port of India.

Corporatized port of India:

 
• The process of corporatization means that there is a change in legal structure.
 
• It should not be confused with privatization or disinvestment.
 
• Thus, no major impact can be expected by a mere change in the legal structure.
 
• Under the Major Port Trusts Act of 1963, the ports trusts are managed by the Boards of Trustees.
 
• Major Port Authorities Bill 2020 was recently introduced in the Lok Sabha by the Ministry of Shipping.
 
• The Bill aims to replace the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963.
 
• It seeks to provide for the regulation, operation, and planning of Major Ports in India and to vest the administration, control, and management of such ports upon the Boards of Major Port Authorities.
 
• This will empower the Major Ports to perform with greater efficiency on account of full autonomy in decision making and by modernizing the institutional framework of Major Ports.

questions.question: Under the National Waterways Act, 2016, how many inland waterways have been declared as 'national waterways'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**111.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The National Waterways Act, 2016:-**

 
 
• It was enacted to provide for the** development, maintenance, and regulation **of **inland waterways** for **navigation and shipping.**
 
• The Act also provides for the declaration of certain inland waterways as** 'national waterways'** by the** central government, **based on their potential for development and** transportation of goods and passengers.**
 
• The development of **national waterways** is expected to boost **inland water transport, reduce transportation costs,** and promote** economic growth and regional connectivity.**
 
• **111 inland waterways have been declared as 'national waterways' under the National Waterways Act, 2016.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inland waterways:-**

 
 
• These​ are water bodies such as** rivers, canals, lakes, and lagoons** that are used for t**ransportation, recreation, irrigation,** and other purposes.
 
• The development of inland waterways has been a priority for the **Indian government** to reduce congestion on** roads and railways, promote sustainable transportation**, and enhance **trade and tourism.**
 
• Some of the major national waterways in India include the **Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system**, the** Brahmaputra river**, the **West Coast Canal in Kerala**, and the **Godavari-Krishna river system** in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
 
• The development of national waterways involves various activities such as **dredging, construction of terminals, jetties, and navigational aids**, and provision of facilities for cargo and passenger handling.
